risks: Low: both arms receive active diabetes care; group visits may expose personal results to other patients.
consent: Written informed consent after an information sheet; group participants agree to keep other members' information confidential; patients can switch to individual reviews at any time.
data: Pseudonymised trial database held by the practice network's research team; routine laboratory results extracted with consent.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients with limited English, shift work or caring duties attend least. Sessions are offered in the evening with interpreting, and attendance and outcomes are reported by age, work status and language.
effectiveness: The trial tells the partners whether expansion is worth it.
efficiency: Group visits may save clinician time if sessions are full; the trial records nurse time.
costs: Research nurse time for recruitment and data collection, not yet funded.
grants: A primary care research grant would be needed; none is in place.
partnerships: Neighbouring practices, the local diabetes specialist nurse team, and two patients with type 2 diabetes as advisers.
rebPath: Full research ethics review under ICH-GCP and the Declaration of Helsinki, and registration in a public trial registry before recruitment; neither has been started.
limitations: Unblinded delivery, possible contamination, and dependence on neighbouring practices joining.
summary: Low-risk trial with consent, confidentiality rules for groups and equity measures; funding, practices and approvals are not yet in place.
